title: China's AI chipmakers raise prices as high-bandwidth memory shortage bites
key_facts: Huawei lifted the indicated price of its Ascend 950DT card to above 250,000 yuan, a 20% to 50% rise from two months ago.
Cambricon's next-generation chip (tentatively the 690) is priced 20% to 30% above levels indicated two months ago.
MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX made similar increases.
The sources blame a worldwide HBM shortage; memory is a large share of an accelerator's production cost.
Since US controls tightened in December 2024, Chinese chipmakers rely on grey-market HBM that typically costs several times what buyers outside China pay.
Huawei's Ascend 950PR went from about 60,000 yuan at the start of the year to over 80,000 yuan.
quote_evidence: Chinese AI chipmakers including Huawei Technologies and Cambricon have sharply raised prices for current and next-generation AI processors, three people familiar with the matter said, as soaring costs for high-bandwidth memory squeeze efforts to build domestic alternatives to Nvidia.
The people declined to be identified because the pricing discussions are not public.
Huawei, Cambricon, MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX did not respond to requests for comment.
why_it_matters_hint: Memory shortage and export controls raise the cost of China's domestic AI chips.
notes: The Standard's text reads like a wire report but does not name another outlet, so The Standard is credited. Companies did not respond to requests for comment. Search found no other outlet carrying it.
